before.name: B. Kwaku Duren
before.description: B. Kwaku Duren, also known as Bob Duren and Robert Donaldson Duren, was coordinator of the Southern California chapter of the Black Panther Party from 1976 to 1981 and a co-chair of the Coalition Against Police Abuse. Los Angeles police repeatedly arrested him during his organizing work, including on allegations of resisting arrest, inciting a riot and marijuana possession. The available reports do not provide complete booking and release dates for those arrests or establish a custodial sentence.

before.name: Mary Crow Dog
before.description: Mary Crow Dog, later Mary Brave Bird, was a Sicangu (Brulé) Lakota AIM activist from the Rosebud Reservation and author of the American Book Award–winning memoir "Lakota Woman." She joined the American Indian Movement as a teenager and gave birth to her son during the 1973 occupation of Wounded Knee, for which she was arrested and briefly jailed. She later married the medicine man Leonard Crow Dog and continued writing and activism until her death in 2013.
